tools.name: request_draft
tools.description: Present how you read the user's request as a JSON draft and wait for an interactive user to accept, edit or decline it. Call it alone before starting work when the request could reasonably be read in more than one way, or when a wrong reading would waste the turn. The backend will defer other calls from the same response until after the decision and a fresh plan. Without an interactive client, the backend accepts the draft after its configured headless timeout. The result carries `decision` (accept = proceed as drafted, update = proceed with `draft`, the user's edited version, decline = do not proceed), `status` (answered, timed_out or cancelled) and, when the user changed something, `changed` — the paths they added, removed or corrected. Treat decline, timeout or cancellation as no approval; do not proceed.

title.description: One line naming what the draft decides, shown above it.

draft.description: Your structured understanding: the fields the user should confirm or correct (goal, scope, constraints, assumptions, open questions, …). Any shape is allowed; keep it small enough to read at a glance.
